definitions.explanation: Used to refer to oneself in a boastful or domineering way.

examples.japanese: {俺様|おれさま}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{任|まか}せろ→任せる：02417_makaseru⟧。
examples.english: Leave it to the great me.

examples.japanese: {俺様|おれさま}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{逆|さか}らう→逆らう：02106_sakarau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧？
⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{俺様|おれさま}⟦キャラ→キャラ：08916_kyara⟧だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{付|つ}き{合|あ}い→付き合う：02291_tsukiau⟧にくい。
examples.english: He's the arrogant type, so he's hard to get along with.

notes:
A combination of ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧ (I, masculine informal) and ⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧ (honorific suffix). Using an honorific on oneself is inherently arrogant, so this pronoun conveys extreme self-importance. In real life, it is rarely used seriously and often appears in fiction (manga, anime, games) for villains or arrogant characters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {俺様|おれさま}⟦キャラ→キャラ：08916_kyara⟧: an arrogant character type
- {俺様|おれさま}⟦{気質|きしつ}→気質：13256_kishitsu⟧: domineering temperament
- {俺様|おれさま}⟦{系|けい}→〜系：28466_kei⟧: the arrogant-guy type

USAGE:
In modern slang, {俺様|おれさま} is commonly used as a modifier to describe a personality type: someone who is self-centered, bossy, and domineering. The term {俺様|おれさま}⟦キャラ→キャラ：08916_kyara⟧ is widely used in discussions of fiction and personality types.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧: I (masculine, informal) — the standard casual masculine pronoun without the arrogant connotation
- {我輩|わがはい}: I (pompous, literary) — an old-fashioned self-important pronoun, famously used in ⟦{夏目漱石|なつめそうせき}→夏目漱石：30575_natsumesouseki⟧'s novel title
